summary_rationale: JPMorgan Chase & Co. operates the widest-moat, highest-return universal banking franchise in the United States. It generated $182.45 billion in FY2025 GAAP net revenue ($57.05 billion net income) and $157.36 billion in 9M 2026 net revenue ($52.95 billion net income). Q3 2026 ROTCE reached 20% reported (21% adjusted) on a 14.0% Standardized and Advanced CET1 ratio ($304.1 billion CET1). Its four pillars—CCB, CIB, AWM ($5.21 trillion AUM / $7.90 trillion client assets at Q3 2026), and Corporate Treasury—pair a 2.13% interest-bearing deposit cost with $17B+ annual tech spend to compound TBVPS ($112.64 in Q3 2026). Key refreshed watches are material but manageable rather than thesis-breaking: FY2026 adjusted expenses rising toward ~$108.6 billion (54% Q3 overhead ratio), a -$19.82 billion AOCI deficit alongside $25.84 billion in unrecorded HTM unrealized losses, ~$24 billion / $106.7 billion in Apple Card off-balance-sheet commitments ($2.3 billion pre-closing reserve), $449.1 billion in non-bank/asset-manager/SPE wholesale exposure, the 5.5% 2028 G-SIB surcharge and March 2026 Basel III Re-Proposal (~6% CET1 lift), an August–September 2026 buyback pause, and multi-seat executive transitions (Marianne Lake retired, Petno/Rohrbaugh elected Co-Presidents, and CFO Jeremy Barnum handing off to Bregje de Best post-Q1 2027).
